note: One baseline for one config. Re-recorded 2026-09-15 on the upgrade to kinemata 0.1.0; the expiry is DELIBERATELY left at the previous record's 2026-09-22, so nothing already accepted gains a longer life than it had. The 0.1.1 upgrade did NOT re-record: all four gates read rc 0 with no new finding, so a record would have added nothing and would have reset that expiry. The 0.1.2 upgrade did not re-record either, on the same ground and a stronger reading of it: all four gates read rc 0 with output byte-identical to what 0.1.1 printed on this tree, so there was not merely no new finding but no new line. The 0.2.0 upgrade did not re-record either, and it is the first that could not rest on byte-identity: `claims` gains a `negated:` line by design, and `claims -v` gains the sites under it. That line is not a finding -- it is a disclosure of path claims the tool had been withdrawing from checking silently -- so all four gates still read rc 0 with nothing new accepted, and a record would again have added nothing while resetting the expiry. Five residues, all reported rather than tuned away, per [R159]. (1) REGISTRY: the duplication findings check still reports -- second spellings of declared constants, including the settings_launch.py BoxMode site that is a deliberate floor-module exception and belongs here with that reason rather than in an exclude line that would also hide the next real one. (2) PARITY: the two unproduced identifiers on the categories registry, scopes and scopes_spec. They are metadata sitting inside the manifest's table of categories rather than categories themselves, so the manifest declares eleven keys where the code declares nine delivery families. The fix is a manifest-and-spec question, not a config one; filtering them out of the registry would make the check agree with itself and report nothing. (3) CLAIMS: the documentation residue, the bulk of it runtime and host-store path claims naming paths in the tree kanibako creates for a user rather than in this repo -- not history, and not excludable by file. Dating them is the tool's own designed answer and is preferred to pretending they are false. From 0.1.2 it is no longer the only designed answer: the illustration role :shown:, until then honored in docstrings alone, now marks a span in markdown too, and a marked span is not read as a claim at all. The appeal is real and it is asymmetric -- dating lapses by construction where a mark suppresses permanently -- and it would reach very nearly every finding accepted here, the whole claims-side population of this baseline, which is the same population whether it is counted in findings or in ENTRIES. NO COMMAND PRINTS THAT FIGURE, and this sentence asserted that `claims` prints it until 2026-09-19, when the claim was checked and found false at 0.1.2 and 0.2.0 alike, plain and `-v`. It is a derivation from cover lines rather than a number anything reports: `kinemata claims` accounts for the claims-side records across two of its own figures, those still accepted as pre-existing and those no longer present, while `kinemata check` reports the same population from the other side as the further findings belonging to `claims`, with the two `parity` residues counted in alongside them. Run them and do the arithmetic rather than quoting a number from here; STATE THE BASELINE WITH ANY COUNT applies to it as much as to any other. It was considered and DECLINED on 2026-09-18, and the reason is not the render cost: these spans name kanibako's OWN runtime filenames, box.yaml and workset.yaml and vault/, which we rename, and a marked span is blind to the next rename. Dating keeps them under review, which is what an expiry is for. So dating remains what this baseline does, no document in this tree marks a span with the role, and the decision is recorded on the board rather than here -- FYI to Jei, not a gate, and one word overturns it. Nothing in llm-docs/ or api-docs/ is excluded; those findings are real and are accepted by date, not suppressed. (4) CLAIMS, NEW AT 0.1.0 AND THE REASON FOR THIS RE-RECORD: 44 further claims of that same kind became visible when 0.1.0 fixed a negation window that had been silently swallowing them -- the distance bound was measured per line and the two concatenated, and a full stop did not end a negation's clause. They are NOT new text. Four were read at source before accepting any of them: MIGRATION.md:77, :2958, :5510 and llm-docs/kanibako/project/workset.py.md:47, every one prose naming a box-store runtime file that resolves in no tree. The fix discriminates both ways here -- the genuinely negated claims stayed suppressed -- so this block is the designed answer, not a workaround. CONDITION RETIRED BY kinemata 0.1.1, AND THE HISTORY IS KEPT BECAUSE A READER WHO SEES THE SYMPTOM STILL NEEDS ITS SHAPE: 0.1.0 matched the gitignored path fragments git returns as unanchored substrings of tracked paths, so any tracked file whose path contained such a fragment fell out of the file index. An empty .claude/ at the repo root was enough -- the fragment is .claude, and the worktrees/ child this note first blamed had nothing to do with it -- and it dropped the tracked, shipped .claude/settings.json, which made this count read 46 rather than 44. The directory was moved aside and the defect reported upstream. 0.1.1 fixes the matching: the directory is RESTORED, and the run that read 44 without it reads 44 with it. STATE THE BASELINE WITH ANY COUNT -- 44 and 46 are against the baseline this record replaced, not against this one, and a finding count is a property of a tree-and-baseline pair rather than of the tree. (5) CLAIMS, NEW AT 0.2.0, AND ACCEPTED BY NOTHING HERE: path claims on this tree are withdrawn from checking by a negation in the same clause, and until 0.2.0 nothing said so -- a run that lost claims that way was indistinguishable from a clean one. `negated:` now prints the size of it and `claims -v` lists every site. They enter no baseline and no expiry, because they are not findings: they are coverage this gate was never buying, and the only answer to them is reading the sentences, which a separate pass is doing. Upstream measured before building and shipped listing rather than tuning the negation word list, because no negation word is reliably wrong across trees -- `had` withdrew four claims on their tree, every one of them naming a path that resolves, and four on ours, none of which did. STATE THE BASELINE WITH ANY COUNT applies here and doubly: upstream published a companion figure counting how many withdrawn claims resolve, then withdrew it rather than correcting it, because a path claim resolves by basename and a withdrawn token can therefore match an unrelated file anywhere in the tree. Resolving is a weak proxy for should-have-been-checked. The negation rule itself is unchanged at 0.2.0.
